अश्ममयीनां पारे यत् किंचासुराणां वामं वसु तेन तिष्ठति तं जहि य एष कृच्छ्रे हन्तावोचथा इति तम् इन्द्रो दाल्भूष्याभिविसृज्य पराभिनत् सो ऽब्रवीद् एष हतस् तम् आहर य एष कृच्छ्राद् आहर्तावोचथा इति तं विष्णुर् अपासङ्ग आहरत् । यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् । यज्ञेनैवैषां तद् यज्ञम् अवृञ्जत पशुभिः पशून् इन्द्रियेणेन्द्रियम् । ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा अभवन् यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् । यज्ञेनैवैतद् यज्ञं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते पशुभिः पशून् इन्द्रियेणेन्द्रियम् । भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति देवयजनम् इच्छन्ति यज्ञम् एवेच्छन्ति यद् विन्दन्ति यज्ञम् एव विन्दन्ति यद् उदीचीनं प्राचीनं प्रवणं स्यात् तस्मिन् यजेत यज्ञकामस् । एवम् एव हि स यज्ञो ऽशयत् । यज्ञस्यानुवित्त्यै यत् समं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्मिन् यजेत गतश्रीः प्रतिष्ठा वा एतस्मा एष्टव्या यो गतश्रीर् एतद् भूम्याः प्रतिष्ठितं यत् समम् । प्रतिष्ठाम् एवास्मै विन्दति गच्छति प्रतिष्ठाम् । त्र्युन्नते यजेत भ्रातृव्यवान् । त्र्युन्नतेन वै विष्णुर् इमांल् लोकान् उदजयत् स एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ऽसुरान् प्राणुदत । इमान् एव लोकान् उज्जयति । एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो भ्रातृव्यं प्रणुदते । यस्यैकधा मध्य उन्नतं स्यात् तस्मिन् यजेत स्वर्गकामस् । अतो वै देवास् स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै यत्रौषधयो बह्वीर् अन्या अन्या इव स्युस् तस्मिन् यजेत पशुकामस् । ओषधयो वै पशवस् । भूमानम् एव पशूनाम् उपैति यत्रौषधयः कृच्छ्रशः पर्यायशः परीयुस् तस्मिन् यजेत पशुकामस् । अतो वै देवाः पशून् उदसृजन्त पशून् एवोत्सृजते यद् ऋक्षम् अलोमकं तस्मिन् याजयेद् यं द्विष्यात् । व्यृद्धं वा एतद् ओषधिभिर् यद् ऋक्षम् अलोमकम् ओषधयः पशवः पशुभिर् एवैनं व्यर्धयति । यत् समया देवयजनं पन्था विधावेत् तस्मिन् याजयेद् यं कामयेत व्य् एनं प्रजया पशुभिश् छिन्द्याम् इति । एतद् वै विच्छिन्नं नाम देवयजनम् । व्य् एनं प्रजया पशुभिश् छिनत्ति यद् अन्तरापश् च देवयजनं च पन्था विधावेत् तस्मिन् याजयेद् यं कामयेत नैनम् अपरो यज्ञ उपनमेद् इति । एतद् वै परिवर्त्म नाम देवयजनम् । पर्य् एणम् अपरो यज्ञो वृणक्ति यत्रापस् सर्वतस् समवद् रवेयुस् तस्मिन् यजेतान्नकामस् । दिग्भ्यो वा एतस्मा अन्नं हरन्ति यस्मै हरन्त्य् आपो ऽन्नम् । सर्वाभ्य एव दिग्भ्यो ऽन्नाद्यम् अवरुन्द्धे तद् एतत् समापं नाम देवयजनम् । नीपतमम् इवर्तसमानानां भवति ।
25.2.m:
The gods and the Asuras indeed were in conflict over the sacrifice.
That sacrifice was afraid: ‘Whichever will conquer, they will tear me apart.’
It hid itself.
The gods, having conquered, searched for it.
They went seeking side by side.
Indra stepped right over it.
It said: ‘Who is this that has stepped right over me?’
‘I am he who strikes in difficulty.’
‘Then who are you?’
‘I am he who brings back from difficulty.’
‘This boar, Emūṣa by name,’ he said, ‘stands on the other side of twenty-one stone strongholds with whatever lovely wealth belongs to the Asuras. Slay him, you who declared: "I strike in difficulty"!’
Indra, shooting at him with a reed-stalk, split him apart.
He said: ‘He is slain; bring him back, you who declared: "I bring back from difficulty"!’
Viṣṇu, the Apāsaṅga, brought him back.
Viṣṇu is indeed the sacrifice.
By the sacrifice they thus wrested their sacrifice, with animals [their] animals, with faculty [their] faculty.
Then the gods prospered; the Asuras were vanquished.
Viṣṇu is indeed the sacrifice.
By the sacrifice he thus wrests the sacrifice of his rival, with animals [his] animals, with faculty [his] faculty.
He prospers in himself; his rival is vanquished.
They seek a place for worship of the gods;
they seek the sacrifice itself.
When they find [it],
they find the sacrifice itself.
If it slopes towards the north and east, one who desires sacrifice should sacrifice on it;
for in just this manner that sacrifice lay,
for the finding of the sacrifice.
One who has attained prosperity should sacrifice on what is level and firmly established.
A firm foundation indeed should be sought for him who has attained prosperity;
this is the firm foundation of the earth: what is level.
He finds a firm foundation for him; he goes to a firm foundation.
One who has a rival should sacrifice on [ground that is] raised in three places.
By [ground] raised in three places Viṣṇu conquered these worlds;
he drove the Asuras out from these worlds.
He conquers these very worlds;
he drives out his rival from these worlds.
One desiring heaven should sacrifice on that whose center is raised uniformly.
From here indeed the gods went to the world of heaven,
for the attainment of the world of heaven.
One desiring animals should sacrifice where plants are many and varied, as it were.
Plants are indeed animals;
he attains an abundance of animals.
One desiring animals should sacrifice where plants grow in thickets and cycles.
From here indeed the gods sent forth animals;
he sends forth animals.
On what is barren and bare of hair he should cause him to sacrifice whom he hates.
Deprived of plants indeed is what is barren and bare of hair;
plants are animals;
he deprives him of animals.
On [a site] through the middle of which a road runs, he should cause him to sacrifice of whom he might wish: ‘May I cut him off from offspring and animals.’
This indeed is the place for worship of the gods called ‘severed’;
he cuts him off from offspring and animals.
On [a site] between which and the waters a road runs, he should cause him to sacrifice of whom he might wish: ‘Let no further sacrifice turn toward him.’
This indeed is the place for worship of the gods called ‘encircled by a road’;
further sacrifice passes around him.
One desiring food should sacrifice where waters flow together from all sides.
They bring food from the quarters to him for whom waters bring food;
he secures edible food from all quarters.
This is the place for worship of the gods called ‘converging waters’;
it is, as it were, the lowest of those of equal season.

25.3.s: yatrāpaḥ prācīr āhavanīyāt pratīcīr gārhapatyād vyavadraveyus tasmin yājayed yam udake vā pātre vā vivāhe vā mīmāṃseran pāpmanā vā eṣo 'nuṣakto yam udake vā pātre vā vivāhe vā mīmāṃsante pāpmanaivainaṃ vyāvartayati yatrāpo dakṣiṇā pariplūya paścātprācī rameraṃs tasmin yajeta bubhūṣan | āpo vai sarvā devatās | etad devatābhir juṣṭaṃ devayajanam | yad evaṃ devatābhir eva juṣṭe devayajane yajate bhavaty eva yatrāpo dakṣiṇata udīcī rameraṃs tasmin yajeta sajātakāmas | āpo vai sarvā devatās devatās sajātās sajātānām evainaṃ prārdhe karoti kṛtrime yajeta bubhūṣan | ātmā vai devayajanam | karoty evainam | yatrāgniṃ cāpaś ca paśyan prātaranuvākam anubrūyāt tasmin yajeta yaḥ kāmayeta yajño māpara upanamed iti | agnir vai sarvā devatā āpo yajñas | upainam aparo yajño namati devatāś ca hi yajñaṃ ca paśyan yajate yatrāgnim apas sūryaṃ paśyan prātaranuvākam anubrūyāt tasmin yajeta brahmavarcasakāmas | etad vai triśukriyaṃ nāma devayajanam | brahmavarcasī bhavati yat purastād āptaṃ syād devayajanaṃ tasmin yajeta bhrātṛvyavān bhrātṛvyāya vā eṣa loka ucchiṣyate yaḥ purastād devayajanasyocchiṣyata etāvantam evāsmai lokam ucchiṃṣati | alokam enaṃ karoti yo ha vai vidvān devayajanaṃ yajata ṛdhnoti | agnir vāva devayajanam agnau hi sarvā devatā ijyante yatraiva kvacāgnim ādhāya yajeta tenaivardhnoti brāhmaṇā vāva devayajanam | yatra brāhmaṇā bahavas saṃrādhayeyus tasmin yajeta tenaivardhnoti |
25.3.d: यत्रापः प्राचीर् आहवनीयात् प्रतीचीर् गार्हपत्याद् व्यवद्रवेयुस् तस्मिन् याजयेद् यम् उदके वा पात्रे वा विवाहे वा मीमांसेरन् पाप्मना वा एषो ऽनुषक्तो यम् उदके वा पात्रे वा विवाहे वा मीमांसन्ते पाप्मनैवैनं व्यावर्तयति यत्रापो दक्षिणा परिप्लूय पश्चात्प्राची रमेरंस् तस्मिन् यजेत बुभूषन् । आपो वै सर्वा देवतास् । एतद् देवताभिर् जुष्टं देवयजनम् । यद् एवं देवताभिर् एव जुष्टे देवयजने यजते भवत्य् एव यत्रापो दक्षिणत उदीची रमेरंस् तस्मिन् यजेत सजातकामस् । आपो वै सर्वा देवतास् देवतास् सजातास् सजातानाम् एवैनं प्रार्धे करोति कृत्रिमे यजेत बुभूषन् । आत्मा वै देवयजनम् । करोत्य् एवैनम् । यत्राग्निं चापश् च पश्यन् प्रातरनुवाकम् अनुब्रूयात् तस्मिन् यजेत यः कामयेत यज्ञो मापर उपनमेद् इति । अग्निर् वै सर्वा देवता आपो यज्ञस् । उपैनम् अपरो यज्ञो नमति देवताश् च हि यज्ञं च पश्यन् यजते यत्राग्निम् अपस् सूर्यं पश्यन् प्रातरनुवाकम् अनुब्रूयात् तस्मिन् यजेत ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस् । एतद् वै त्रिशुक्रियं नाम देवयजनम् । ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति यत् पुरस्ताद् आप्तं स्याद् देवयजनं तस्मिन् यजेत भ्रातृव्यवान् भ्रातृव्याय वा एष लोक उच्छिष्यते यः पुरस्ताद् देवयजनस्योच्छिष्यत एतावन्तम् एवास्मै लोकम् उच्छिंषति । अलोकम् एनं करोति यो ह वै विद्वान् देवयजनं यजत ऋध्नोति । अग्निर् वाव देवयजनम् अग्नौ हि सर्वा देवता इज्यन्ते यत्रैव क्वचाग्निम् आधाय यजेत तेनैवर्ध्नोति ब्राह्मणा वाव देवयजनम् । यत्र ब्राह्मणा बहवस् संराधयेयुस् तस्मिन् यजेत तेनैवर्ध्नोति ।
25.3.m:
Where waters would run apart eastward from the Āhavanīya and westward from the Gārhapatya, on that [ground] he should sacrifice for one about whom people would investigate concerning water, vessels, or marriage.
He is indeed tied to evil about whom people investigate concerning water, vessels, or marriage.
By evil indeed he separates him [from it].
Where waters, having flowed around to the south, rest facing eastward behind, on that [ground] one should sacrifice who desires to prosper.
All deities are the waters.
This is a place for worship of the gods favored by the deities.
When one sacrifices on a place for worship of the gods favored by the deities,
he indeed prospers.
Where waters rest north from the south, on that [ground] one should sacrifice who desires kinsmen.
The waters are all the deities.
The deities are kinsmen.
He places him right at the head of the kinsmen.
One desiring to prosper should sacrifice on an artificial [ground].
The self is the place for worship of the gods.
He indeed makes it [prosper].
Where, seeing both fire and waters, he would recite the morning litany, on that [ground] one should sacrifice who wishes: 'May another sacrifice approach me.'
Agni is all the deities; the waters are the sacrifice.
Another sacrifice approaches him;
for he sacrifices seeing both the deities and the sacrifice.
Where, seeing fire, waters, and the sun, he would recite the morning litany, on that [ground] one should sacrifice who desires sacred splendor.
This indeed is the place for worship of the gods called Triśukriya.
He becomes endowed with sacred splendor.
Where the place for worship of the gods is enclosed in front, on that [ground] one who has a rival should sacrifice.
For a rival indeed this world is left over.
Whatever is left over in front of the place for worship of the gods, just so much world he leaves over for him;
he makes him worldless.
He who, knowing thus, sacrifices on a place for worship of the gods thrives.
Agni is indeed the place for worship of the gods;
for in Agni all deities are sacrificed to.
Wherever he may sacrifice having established the fire,
through that alone he thrives.
The Brahmins are indeed the place for worship of the gods.
Where many Brahmins would accomplish [the rite] together, on that [ground] he should sacrifice;
through that alone he thrives.

25.4.s: vediṃ vimimīte triṃśatā paścāt prakramair mimīte ṣaṭtriṃśatā prācīṃ caturviṃśatyā purastāt | virājaivaināṃ paścāt parimimīte bṛhatyā prācīṃ gāyatryā purastāt | chandobhir evaināṃ sarvataḥ parimimīte virājy eva pratitiṣṭhati yad virājam abhisaṃpādayati sphyena stambayajur harati | indro vai vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat sa tredhābhavat sphyas tṛtīyaṃ yūpas tṛtīyaṃ rathas tṛtīyam | vajro vai sphyas | etāvatī pṛthivī yāvatī vedis | vajreṇaiva pṛthivyā bhrātṛvyaṃ nirbhajati trir harati traya ime lokās | ebhya evainaṃ lokebhyo nirbhajati | tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ harati | aparimitād evainaṃ nirbhajati | indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā tam anayābhinyadadhāt | yaṃ tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ haraty anayaiva bhrātṛvyam abhinidadhāti mūlaṃ chinatti bhrātṛvyasyaiva mūlaṃ chinatti | uddhanti tasmāc chiśira oṣadhayaḥ parābhavanti barhis stṛṇāti tasmād vasantā punar ābhavanti | apārarum adevayajanaṃ pṛthivyā devayajanāj jahīti bhrātṛvyo vā ararus | bhrātṛvyam eva pṛthivyā apahanti drapsas te dyāṃ mā skān iti yo vā asyā rasas sa drapsas tam imāḥ prajā upajīvanti tam evāsyāṃ yacchati tasyāskandāya | ararur dyāṃ mā paptad iti bhrātṛvyo vā ararus | bhrātṛvyam eva svargāl lokāt pratinudate | viṣād vai nāmāsura āsīt sa pṛthivīṃ viṣeṇālimpat tasyā na kaścanāśnāt | ya āśnāt so 'rupyat | yad uddhanti yad evāsyā amedhyam ayajñiyaṃ tad apahanti | api mūlam anukhanet | āviddhasya niṣkṛtyai | adho dūraṃ khanet | adho vā asyā vīryam | vīryasyābhitṛttyai tasmāt sukṛṣṭe vrīhiyavāḥ pacyante tad āhus | uttarārdhe vā asyā vīryaṃ tad imāḥ prajā upajīvanti tasmān nātikheyeti | ā pratiṣṭhāyāḥ khanet | yajamānasya pratiṣṭhityai dakṣiṇata udvanāṃ kuryāt | devayajanasya rūpam | rakṣasām apahatyai purīṣavatīm | paśavo vai purīṣaṃ paśūn evāvarunddhe |
25.4.d: वेदिं विमिमीते त्रिंशता पश्चात् प्रक्रमैर् मिमीते षट्त्रिंशता प्राचीं चतुर्विंशत्या पुरस्तात् । विराजैवैनां पश्चात् परिमिमीते बृहत्या प्राचीं गायत्र्या पुरस्तात् । छन्दोभिर् एवैनां सर्वतः परिमिमीते विराज्य् एव प्रतितिष्ठति यद् विराजम् अभिसंपादयति स्फ्येन स्तम्बयजुर् हरति । इन्द्रो वै वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरत् स त्रेधाभवत् स्फ्यस् तृतीयं यूपस् तृतीयं रथस् तृतीयम् । वज्रो वै स्फ्यस् । एतावती पृथिवी यावती वेदिस् । वज्रेणैव पृथिव्या भ्रातृव्यं निर्भजति त्रिर् हरति त्रय इमे लोकास् । एभ्य एवैनं लोकेभ्यो निर्भजति । तूष्णीं चतुर्थं हरति । अपरिमिताद् एवैनं निर्भजति । इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा तम् अनयाभिन्यदधात् । यं तूष्णीं चतुर्थं हरत्य् अनयैव भ्रातृव्यम् अभिनिदधाति मूलं छिनत्ति भ्रातृव्यस्यैव मूलं छिनत्ति । उद्धन्ति तस्माच् छिशिर ओषधयः पराभवन्ति बर्हिस् स्तृणाति तस्माद् वसन्ता पुनर् आभवन्ति । अपाररुम् अदेवयजनं पृथिव्या देवयजनाज् जहीति भ्रातृव्यो वा अररुस् । भ्रातृव्यम् एव पृथिव्या अपहन्ति द्रप्सस् ते द्यां मा स्कान् इति यो वा अस्या रसस् स द्रप्सस् तम् इमाः प्रजा उपजीवन्ति तम् एवास्यां यच्छति तस्यास्कन्दाय । अररुर् द्यां मा पप्तद् इति भ्रातृव्यो वा अररुस् । भ्रातृव्यम् एव स्वर्गाल् लोकात् प्रतिनुदते । विषाद् वै नामासुर आसीत् स पृथिवीं विषेणालिम्पत् तस्या न कश्चनाश्नात् । य आश्नात् सो ऽरुप्यत् । यद् उद्धन्ति यद् एवास्या अमेध्यम् अयज्ञियं तद् अपहन्ति । अपि मूलम् अनुखनेत् । आविद्धस्य निष्कृत्यै । अधो दूरं खनेत् । अधो वा अस्या वीर्यम् । वीर्यस्याभितृत्त्यै तस्मात् सुकृष्टे व्रीहियवाः पच्यन्ते तद् आहुस् । उत्तरार्धे वा अस्या वीर्यं तद् इमाः प्रजा उपजीवन्ति तस्मान् नातिखेयेति । आ प्रतिष्ठायाः खनेत् । यजमानस्य प्रतिष्ठित्यै दक्षिणत उद्वनां कुर्यात् । देवयजनस्य रूपम् । रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै पुरीषवतीम् । पशवो वै पुरीषं पशून् एवावरुन्द्धे ।
25.4.m:
He measures out the altar.
He measures it behind with thirty steps, thirty-six toward the east, twenty-four in front.
With the Virāj he measures it behind, with the Bṛhatī toward the east, with the Gāyatrī in front.
With the meters indeed he measures it on all sides.
He is established in the Virāj when he brings about the Virāj.
With the wooden sword he takes the grass-clump offering.
Indra hurled the vajra at Vṛtra.
It became threefold:
the wooden sword a third, the sacrificial post a third, the chariot a third.
The wooden sword is the vajra.
As great as the altar is, so great is the earth.
With the vajra he excludes the rival from the earth.
Three times he takes it.
Three are these worlds.
From these worlds he excludes him.
Silently he takes it the fourth time.
From the unlimited he excludes him.
Indra, having slain Vṛtra, covered him with this [earth].
When he takes it silently the fourth time, with this [earth] he covers the rival.
He cuts the root;
he cuts the root of the rival.
He digs up [the ground];
therefore in the cold season plants perish.
He strews the sacrificial grass;
therefore in spring they come into being again.
'Strike away from the earth's place for worship of the gods the non-worshipping Araru!'
Araru is the rival;
he strikes the rival away from the earth.
'May thy drop not leap to heaven!'
What is its sap, that is the drop;
upon that these creatures subsist.
That alone he secures in her,
so that it will not spill.
'May Araru not fly to heaven!'
Araru is the rival;
he repels the rival from the heavenly world.
There was an Asura named Viṣād;
he smeared the earth with poison.
No one ate of it;
whoever ate fell sick.
When he digs up [the ground],
whatever of it is impure, unfit for sacrifice, that he strikes away.
He should also dig along the root,
for the repair of what is pierced.
He should dig deep below;
below indeed is its vigor,
for the piercing of the vigor.
Therefore in well-plowed [ground] rice and barley ripen.
Concerning this they say:
'In its northern half is its vigor; upon that these creatures subsist; therefore one should not dig too deeply.'
He should dig up to the firm foundation,
for the firm foundation of the sacrificer.
He should make it sloping to the south,
[which is] the form of the place for worship of the gods,
for the striking away of the Rakṣases;
[and] rich in earth.
Cattle are earth;
he gains cattle.

25.5.s: sphyena vediṃ parigṛhṇāti vajro vai sphyas | etāvatī pṛthivī yāvatī vedir vajreṇaiva pṛthivyā bhrātṛvyaṃ nirbhajya cchandobhir ātmane parigṛhṇāti vasavas tvā parigṛhṇantu gāyatreṇa cchandaseti dakṣiṇatas tejo vai brahma gāyatrī tejasaivaināṃ dakṣiṇataḥ parigṛhṇāti rudrās tvā parigṛhṇantu triṣṭubhena cchandaseti paścāt | ojo vai vīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasaivaināṃ paścāt parigṛhṇāti | ādityās tvā parigṛhṇantu jāgatena cchandasety uttarāt | jāgatā vai paśava uttarādāyatanāḥ paśavaḥ paśubhya evaitad āyatanaṃ karoti paśūnāṃ dhṛtyai | atho tejasā cobhayataḥ paśūn parigṛhṇāti purā krūrasya visṛpo virapśinn iti yad vā asyās tejo yajñiyaṃ tad adaś candramasi tad evāvarunddhe | idhmābarhiṣī prokṣati śuṣkāṇī vā etāny amedhyāny āraṇyād āhṛtāny āpo medhyā yajñiyā yad adbhiḥ prokṣati medhye evaine yajñiye karoti vediṃ prokṣati medhyām evaināṃ yajñiyāṃ karoti | atho yad evāsyā udghnantaḥ krūraṃ kurvanti tac chamayati barhis stṛṇāti prajā vai barhiḥ pṛthivī vediḥ prajā eva pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati sarvāṃ vedim anustṛṇāti tasmāt pṛthivīṃ sarvām anv oṣadhayas | bahulaṃ stṛṇīyāt | akṣodhuko yajamāno bhavaty anagnaṃbhāvuko 'dhvaryus | barhiṣi prastaraṃ sādayati yajamāno vai prastaraḥ prajā barhis | yajamānam eva prajāsv adhisādayati | uttaraṃ sādayati | uttaro hi yajamāno 'yajamānāt | vyāvṛttaṃ sādayati vyāvṛtto hi yajamāno 'yajamānena | aktvā prastaraṃ praharati yajamāno vai prastaras | havirbhūtam evainaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati nātyagraṃ praharet | yad atyagraṃ prahared vṛkṇakeśīr janayas syur abhyāsariṇīr naṃśukās | agram agra ādīpayati | agreṇaivāgraṃ samardhayati | ṛjuṃ praharet svargakāmasya | ṛjum evainaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati yaṃ dviṣyāt tasya hūrchayet svargād evainaṃ lokād dhūrchayati | nyañcaṃ prahared vṛṣṭikāmasya yā vā ita āhutir udayate sāmuto vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvayati svayaivāhutyā divo vṛṣṭiṃ ninayati | ūrdhvaṃ prahared yadi kāmayeta pumān asya putro jāyeteti | ūrdhva eva hi pumān prathayitvā prahared yadi kāmayeta strī jāyeteti | evam eva hi strī prathiteva yajamāno vai prastaras | eti vā etad asmāl lokād yat prastaraṃ praharati yat tṛṇam upagṛhṇāti | asminn evainaṃ loke yacchati | anupraharati yad evāsyāvamṛśantaḥ krūraṃ kurvanti yad vicchindantas tac chamayati | agā3n agnī3d iti | agann iti | agan svargaṃ lokam ity evaitad āha śrāvaya śrauṣad iti svargam evainaṃ lokaṃ gataṃ śrāvayati |
25.5.d: स्फ्येन वेदिं परिगृह्णाति वज्रो वै स्फ्यस् । एतावती पृथिवी यावती वेदिर् वज्रेणैव पृथिव्या भ्रातृव्यं निर्भज्य च्छन्दोभिर् आत्मने परिगृह्णाति वसवस् त्वा परिगृह्णन्तु गायत्रेण च्छन्दसेति दक्षिणतस् तेजो वै ब्रह्म गायत्री तेजसैवैनां दक्षिणतः परिगृह्णाति रुद्रास् त्वा परिगृह्णन्तु त्रिष्टुभेन च्छन्दसेति पश्चात् । ओजो वै वीर्यं त्रिष्टुब् ओजसैवैनां पश्चात् परिगृह्णाति । आदित्यास् त्वा परिगृह्णन्तु जागतेन च्छन्दसेत्य् उत्तरात् । जागता वै पशव उत्तरादायतनाः पशवः पशुभ्य एवैतद् आयतनं करोति पशूनां धृत्यै । अथो तेजसा चोभयतः पशून् परिगृह्णाति पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपो विरप्शिन्न् इति यद् वा अस्यास् तेजो यज्ञियं तद् अदश् चन्द्रमसि तद् एवावरुन्द्धे । इध्माबर्हिषी प्रोक्षति शुष्काणी वा एतान्य् अमेध्यान्य् आरण्याद् आहृतान्य् आपो मेध्या यज्ञिया यद् अद्भिः प्रोक्षति मेध्ये एवैने यज्ञिये करोति वेदिं प्रोक्षति मेध्याम् एवैनां यज्ञियां करोति । अथो यद् एवास्या उद्घ्नन्तः क्रूरं कुर्वन्ति तच् छमयति बर्हिस् स्तृणाति प्रजा वै बर्हिः पृथिवी वेदिः प्रजा एव पृथिव्यां प्रतिष्ठापयति सर्वां वेदिम् अनुस्तृणाति तस्मात् पृथिवीं सर्वाम् अन्व् ओषधयस् । बहुलं स्तृणीयात् । अक्षोधुको यजमानो भवत्य् अनग्नंभावुको ऽध्वर्युस् । बर्हिषि प्रस्तरं सादयति यजमानो वै प्रस्तरः प्रजा बर्हिस् । यजमानम् एव प्रजास्व् अधिसादयति । उत्तरं सादयति । उत्तरो हि यजमानो ऽयजमानात् । व्यावृत्तं सादयति व्यावृत्तो हि यजमानो ऽयजमानेन । अक्त्वा प्रस्तरं प्रहरति यजमानो वै प्रस्तरस् । हविर्भूतम् एवैनं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति नात्यग्रं प्रहरेत् । यद् अत्यग्रं प्रहरेद् वृक्णकेशीर् जनयस् स्युर् अभ्यासरिणीर् नंशुकास् । अग्रम् अग्र आदीपयति । अग्रेणैवाग्रं समर्धयति । ऋजुं प्रहरेत् स्वर्गकामस्य । ऋजुम् एवैनं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति यं द्विष्यात् तस्य हूर्छयेत् स्वर्गाद् एवैनं लोकाद् धूर्छयति । न्यञ्चं प्रहरेद् वृष्टिकामस्य या वा इत आहुतिर् उदयते सामुतो वृष्टिं च्यावयति स्वयैवाहुत्या दिवो वृष्टिं निनयति । ऊर्ध्वं प्रहरेद् यदि कामयेत पुमान् अस्य पुत्रो जायेतेति । ऊर्ध्व एव हि पुमान् प्रथयित्वा प्रहरेद् यदि कामयेत स्त्री जायेतेति । एवम् एव हि स्त्री प्रथितेव यजमानो वै प्रस्तरस् । एति वा एतद् अस्माल् लोकाद् यत् प्रस्तरं प्रहरति यत् तृणम् उपगृह्णाति । अस्मिन्न् एवैनं लोके यच्छति । अनुप्रहरति यद् एवास्यावमृशन्तः क्रूरं कुर्वन्ति यद् विच्छिन्दन्तस् तच् छमयति । अगा3न् अग्नी3द् इति । अगन्न् इति । अगन् स्वर्गं लोकम् इत्य् एवैतद् आह श्रावय श्रौषद् इति स्वर्गम् एवैनं लोकं गतं श्रावयति ।
25.5.m:
With the wooden sword he encloses the altar.
The wooden sword is indeed the vajra.
As great as the altar is, so great is the earth.
Having excluded the rival from the earth with the vajra, he encloses it for himself with the meters.
‘May the Vasus enclose you with the Gāyatrī meter,’ [he says] on the south.
The Gāyatrī is indeed brilliance and sacred power.
With brilliance indeed he encloses it on the south.
‘May the Rudras enclose you with the Triṣṭubh meter,’ [he says] behind.
The Triṣṭubh is indeed might and virility.
With might indeed he encloses it behind.
‘May the Ādityas enclose you with the Jagatī meter,’ [he says] from the north.
Cattle belong to the Jagatī; cattle have their abode in the north.
Thus he makes an abode for cattle,
for the stability of cattle.
And on both sides he encloses cattle with brilliance.
‘Before the creeping of the cruel one, O rich one!’ [he says].
Whatever sacrificial brilliance of this [earth] existed, that is yonder in the moon.
He wins that very [brilliance].
He sprinkles the firewood and the sacrificial grass.
Dry and unpurified indeed are these [substances] brought from the forest; the waters are purified and fit for sacrifice.
When he sprinkles with waters,
he makes them both purified and fit for sacrifice.
He sprinkles the altar.
He makes it purified and fit for sacrifice.
And whatever wound they make on it when digging it up, he appeases that.
He strews the sacrificial grass.
The sacrificial grass is offspring, the altar is the earth.
He establishes offspring on the earth.
He strews along the whole altar.
Therefore plants [grow] along the whole earth.
He should strew abundantly.
The sacrificer becomes free from hunger, the Adhvaryu free from nakedness.
He deposits the prastara-bunch on the sacrificial grass.
The prastara-bunch is the sacrificer, the sacrificial grass is offspring.
He places the sacrificer upon the offspring.
He deposits it higher.
For the sacrificer is higher than the non-sacrificer.
He deposits it distinct.
For the sacrificer is distinct from the non-sacrificer.
Having anointed [it], he throws the prastara-bunch forward.
The prastara-bunch is the sacrificer.
Having made him an oblation, he sends him to the heavenly world.
He should not throw it too far forward.
If he were to throw it too far forward, his wives would have their hair torn, wandering about and perishing.
He kindles tip against tip.
Tip by tip indeed he causes it to prosper.
He should throw it straight for one who desires heaven.
He causes him to go straight to the heavenly world.
For one whom he hates, he should make it crooked.
He makes him deviate from the heavenly world.
He should throw it downward for one who desires rain.
The oblation which rises up from here moves the rain down from yonder.
By means of his own oblation he brings down rain from heaven.
He should throw it upright if he should desire that a male son be born to him.
For a male is upright.
Having spread it out he should throw it if he should desire that a female be born.
For a female is spread out, as it were.
The prastara-bunch is the sacrificer.
When he throws forward the prastara-bunch, it indeed departs from this world.
When he takes hold of a blade of grass,
he holds him back in this very world.
He throws [it] along.
Whatever wound they make on it by touching, whatever they cut, he appeases that.
‘Has he gone, O Agnīdh?’ [he says].
‘He has gone,’ [the other responds].
‘He has gone to the heavenly world,’ is what he thereby says.
‘Make [him] hear! May he hear!’ [he says].
He makes it heard that he has gone to the heavenly world.

25.6.s: devāś ca vā asurāś ca saṃyattā āsan | tān yad asyās tejo yajñiyam āsīt tat siṃhīrūpam iva mahiṣīrūpam iva bhūtvāntarātiṣṭhat te 'vidur yatarān vā iyam upāvartsyati ta idaṃ bhaviṣyantīti tāṃ devā upāmantrayanta sābravīd vāryaṃ vṛṇai mām eva pūrvām agner āhutir aśnavātā atha mayā yūyaṃ sarvān kāmān vyaśnavātheti sā devān upāvartata tato devā abhavan parāsurā abhavan yasyaivaṃ viduṣa uttaravedir nyupyate yaś caivaṃ vidvān nivapati bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati daśa paścāt tiraścī padāni bhavanti daśobhayataḥ prācy aparimitā purastād virājā saṃmitā yad vā asurāṇāṃ vittam āsīt tad devā vedyāvindanta tad vedyā veditvam | yad vedyaṃ tad uttaravedyā tad uttaravedyā uttaraveditvam | yasyaivaṃ viduṣo vediś ca kriyata uttaravediś ca nyupyate vittaṃ caiva vedyaṃ ca bhrātṛvyasya vindate prajāpater vai nāsikāśīryata sottaravedir abhavat | yajñaḥ prajāpatis | yad uttaravediṃ nivapati prajāpater eva nāsikāṃ mukhataḥ pratidadhāti catvāri vā etasyā nāmāni nāsikā kaśāris siṃhy uttaravedis taptāyany asīti taptā hy enānait | vittāyany asīti vittā hy enānait | avatān mā nāthitam iti nāthitān hy enān āvat | avatād vyathitam iti vyathitān hy enān āvat | agne aṅgiro yo 'syāṃ pṛthivyām asi yo dvitīyasyāṃ yas tṛtīyasyām iti yad evāsyaiṣu lokeṣu śliṣṭaṃ yan nyaktaṃ tad avarunddhe vided agnir nabho nāmeti | yad vā agner vāmaṃ vasu tan nabhas tenemāṃ pṛthivīṃ prāviśaj jānudaghnam adhas tasmāj jānudaghnaṃ kheyam | tasyaiva vāmasya vasor anuvittyai siṃhy asi mahiṣy asīti siṃhīrūpam iva hi tan mahiṣīrūpam iva bhūtvāntarātiṣṭhat | devebhyaḥ prathasveti prathayaty evainām | devebhyaḥ kalpasveti kalpayaty evainām | devebhyaś śundhasveti śundhaty evainān | devebhyaś śumbhasveti śumbhaty evainām | vibhrāḍ bṛhat pibatu somyaṃ madhv ity antān kalpayati devapātraṃ vā uttaravedis | devapātreṇaiva devatās tarpayati | atho devatābhya eva devapātraṃ nivedayati | yatīn vai sālāvṛkeyā ādan | ta ādīyamānās saṃmṛśyamānā uttaravediṃ samudakrāman | tān nābhyadhṛṣṇuvan | teṣām eko 'smayata tata enān abhyadhṛṣṇuvan | teṣām ekaikam āvarham ādan | tasmān na moghahāsinā bhavyam | yan nissārayati yad evāsyā abhimṛtam amedhyaṃ tan nissārayati prokṣati | etāvatī vā iyaṃ pṛthivy āsīd yāvaty uttaravedis tāṃ samantaṃ rakṣāṃsi saṃprākampanta tāni devā vinudyaitābhir devatābhis samantaṃ parinyadadhur yat prokṣati | etaddevatyā vā imā diśas | rakṣāṃsy eva vinudyaitābhir devatābhis samantam ātmānaṃ parinidadhāti | gopīthāya | etad vā etāṃ pūrvām agner āhutir aśnute yad vyāghārayati | athādo 'bravīn mām eva pūrvām agner āhutir aśnavātā atha mayā yūyaṃ sarvān kāmān vyaśnavātheti | atha vā eṣāṃ tarhy asurās sapatnā āsan | te 'kāmayanta sapatnān sahemahīti siṃhy asi sapatnasāhī svāheti saptnāṃs tenāsahanta te 'kāmayanta paśūn vindemahīti siṃhy asi rāyaspoṣavanis svāheti paśūṃs tenāvindanta te 'kāmayanta prajāṃ vindemahīti siṃhy asi suprajāvanis svāheti prajāṃ tenāvindanta te 'kāmayantādityās syāmeti siṃhy asy ādityavanis svāheti | ādityās tenābhavan | tasmād imā ādityāḥ prajās te 'kāmayanta yajñiyās syāmeti siṃhy asy āvaha devān devāyate yajamānāya svāheti yajñiyās tenābhavan | te 'kāmayanta svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti bhūtebhyas tveti | devā vai bhūtās svargam eva tena lokam āyan yasyaivaṃ viduṣa uttaravedir vyāghāryate yaś caivaṃ vidvān vyāghārayati sarvān evaitayā kāmān vyaśnoti | ime vai lokā adhṛtā āsan | te saṃprākampanta tān devā etair yajurbhir vyaṣṭabhnuvan yad etaiḥ paridhīn paridadhāti | eṣāṃ lokānāṃ vidhṛtyai | agnir vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat sa yāṃ prathamāṃ prāvasat tāṃ paśuṣv avasad vṛṣṇer antarāśṛṅgam | tasmād ūrṇāstukā bhavati yāṃ dvitīyāṃ tāṃ vanaspatiṣu pītudārau tasmāt pītudārur bhavati yāṃ tṛtīyāṃ tām oṣadhiṣu sugandhitejane tasmāt sugandhitejano bhavati yad ete saṃbhārā bhavanti yad evāsyātra śliṣṭaṃ yan nyaktaṃ tad etais saṃbharati sa punar upāvartamānaś śarīram adhūnuta tasya yan māṃsam āsīt tad gulgulv abhavat | yad asthi sa pītudārur yāni lokāni sa sugandhitejanas | yad ete saṃbhārā bhavanti yad evāsyātra śliṣṭaṃ yan nyaktaṃ tad etais saṃbharati | agnes sarvatvāya | agneḥ kulāyam asy agneḥ purīṣam asīti kulāyam iva hy etat purīṣam iva yajñaḥ pratyaṣṭhād iti yajñasya pratiṣṭhityai |
25.6.d: देवाश् च वा असुराश् च संयत्ता आसन् । तान् यद् अस्यास् तेजो यज्ञियम् आसीत् तत् सिंहीरूपम् इव महिषीरूपम् इव भूत्वान्तरातिष्ठत् ते ऽविदुर् यतरान् वा इयम् उपावर्त्स्यति त इदं भविष्यन्तीति तां देवा उपामन्त्रयन्त साब्रवीद् वार्यं वृणै माम् एव पूर्वाम् अग्नेर् आहुतिर् अश्नवाता अथ मया यूयं सर्वान् कामान् व्यश्नवाथेति सा देवान् उपावर्तत ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा अभवन् यस्यैवं विदुष उत्तरवेदिर् न्युप्यते यश् चैवं विद्वान् निवपति भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति दश पश्चात् तिरश्ची पदानि भवन्ति दशोभयतः प्राच्य् अपरिमिता पुरस्ताद् विराजा संमिता यद् वा असुराणां वित्तम् आसीत् तद् देवा वेद्याविन्दन्त तद् वेद्या वेदित्वम् । यद् वेद्यं तद् उत्तरवेद्या तद् उत्तरवेद्या उत्तरवेदित्वम् । यस्यैवं विदुषो वेदिश् च क्रियत उत्तरवेदिश् च न्युप्यते वित्तं चैव वेद्यं च भ्रातृव्यस्य विन्दते प्रजापतेर् वै नासिकाशीर्यत सोत्तरवेदिर् अभवत् । यज्ञः प्रजापतिस् । यद् उत्तरवेदिं निवपति प्रजापतेर् एव नासिकां मुखतः प्रतिदधाति चत्वारि वा एतस्या नामानि नासिका कशारिस् सिंह्य् उत्तरवेदिस् तप्तायन्य् असीति तप्ता ह्य् एनानैत् । वित्तायन्य् असीति वित्ता ह्य् एनानैत् । अवतान् मा नाथितम् इति नाथितान् ह्य् एनान् आवत् । अवताद् व्यथितम् इति व्यथितान् ह्य् एनान् आवत् । अग्ने अङ्गिरो यो ऽस्यां पृथिव्याम् असि यो द्वितीयस्यां यस् तृतीयस्याम् इति यद् एवास्यैषु लोकेषु श्लिष्टं यन् न्यक्तं तद् अवरुन्द्धे विदेद् अग्निर् नभो नामेति । यद् वा अग्नेर् वामं वसु तन् नभस् तेनेमां पृथिवीं प्राविशज् जानुदघ्नम् अधस् तस्माज् जानुदघ्नं खेयम् । तस्यैव वामस्य वसोर् अनुवित्त्यै सिंह्य् असि महिष्य् असीति सिंहीरूपम् इव हि तन् महिषीरूपम् इव भूत्वान्तरातिष्ठत् । देवेभ्यः प्रथस्वेति प्रथयत्य् एवैनाम् । देवेभ्यः कल्पस्वेति कल्पयत्य् एवैनाम् । देवेभ्यश् शुन्धस्वेति शुन्धत्य् एवैनान् । देवेभ्यश् शुम्भस्वेति शुम्भत्य् एवैनाम् । विभ्राड् बृहत् पिबतु सोम्यं मध्व् इत्य् अन्तान् कल्पयति देवपात्रं वा उत्तरवेदिस् । देवपात्रेणैव देवतास् तर्पयति । अथो देवताभ्य एव देवपात्रं निवेदयति । यतीन् वै सालावृकेया आदन् । त आदीयमानास् संमृश्यमाना उत्तरवेदिं समुदक्रामन् । तान् नाभ्यधृष्णुवन् । तेषाम् एको ऽस्मयत तत एनान् अभ्यधृष्णुवन् । तेषाम् एकैकम् आवर्हम् आदन् । तस्मान् न मोघहासिना भव्यम् । यन् निस्सारयति यद् एवास्या अभिमृतम् अमेध्यं तन् निस्सारयति प्रोक्षति । एतावती वा इयं पृथिव्य् आसीद् यावत्य् उत्तरवेदिस् तां समन्तं रक्षांसि संप्राकम्पन्त तानि देवा विनुद्यैताभिर् देवताभिस् समन्तं परिन्यदधुर् यत् प्रोक्षति । एतद्देवत्या वा इमा दिशस् । रक्षांस्य् एव विनुद्यैताभिर् देवताभिस् समन्तम् आत्मानं परिनिदधाति । गोपीथाय । एतद् वा एतां पूर्वाम् अग्नेर् आहुतिर् अश्नुते यद् व्याघारयति । अथादो ऽब्रवीन् माम् एव पूर्वाम् अग्नेर् आहुतिर् अश्नवाता अथ मया यूयं सर्वान् कामान् व्यश्नवाथेति । अथ वा एषां तर्ह्य् असुरास् सपत्ना आसन् । ते ऽकामयन्त सपत्नान् सहेमहीति सिंह्य् असि सपत्नसाही स्वाहेति सप्त्नांस् तेनासहन्त ते ऽकामयन्त पशून् विन्देमहीति सिंह्य् असि रायस्पोषवनिस् स्वाहेति पशूंस् तेनाविन्दन्त ते ऽकामयन्त प्रजां विन्देमहीति सिंह्य् असि सुप्रजावनिस् स्वाहेति प्रजां तेनाविन्दन्त ते ऽकामयन्तादित्यास् स्यामेति सिंह्य् अस्य् आदित्यवनिस् स्वाहेति । आदित्यास् तेनाभवन् । तस्माद् इमा आदित्याः प्रजास् ते ऽकामयन्त यज्ञियास् स्यामेति सिंह्य् अस्य् आवह देवान् देवायते यजमानाय स्वाहेति यज्ञियास् तेनाभवन् । ते ऽकामयन्त स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति भूतेभ्यस् त्वेति । देवा वै भूतास् स्वर्गम् एव तेन लोकम् आयन् यस्यैवं विदुष उत्तरवेदिर् व्याघार्यते यश् चैवं विद्वान् व्याघारयति सर्वान् एवैतया कामान् व्यश्नोति । इमे वै लोका अधृता आसन् । ते संप्राकम्पन्त तान् देवा एतैर् यजुर्भिर् व्यष्टभ्नुवन् यद् एतैः परिधीन् परिदधाति । एषां लोकानां विधृत्यै । अग्निर् वै देवेभ्यो ऽपाक्रामत् स यां प्रथमां प्रावसत् तां पशुष्व् अवसद् वृष्णेर् अन्तराशृङ्गम् । तस्माद् ऊर्णास्तुका भवति यां द्वितीयां तां वनस्पतिषु पीतुदारौ तस्मात् पीतुदारुर् भवति यां तृतीयां ताम् ओषधिषु सुगन्धितेजने तस्मात् सुगन्धितेजनो भवति यद् एते संभारा भवन्ति यद् एवास्यात्र श्लिष्टं यन् न्यक्तं तद् एतैस् संभरति स पुनर् उपावर्तमानश् शरीरम् अधूनुत तस्य यन् मांसम् आसीत् तद् गुल्गुल्व् अभवत् । यद् अस्थि स पीतुदारुर् यानि लोकानि स सुगन्धितेजनस् । यद् एते संभारा भवन्ति यद् एवास्यात्र श्लिष्टं यन् न्यक्तं तद् एतैस् संभरति । अग्नेस् सर्वत्वाय । अग्नेः कुलायम् अस्य् अग्नेः पुरीषम् असीति कुलायम् इव ह्य् एतत् पुरीषम् इव यज्ञः प्रत्यष्ठाद् इति यज्ञस्य प्रतिष्ठित्यै ।
25.6.m:
The gods and the Asuras indeed were in conflict.
Whatever sacrificial brilliance of this [earth] existed, that, having assumed the form of a lioness as it were, the form of a female buffalo as it were, stood between them.
They knew: ‘To whichever [party] she turns, they will become this [all].’
The gods addressed her.
She said: ‘Let me choose a boon: may the oblation reach me before Agni, then through me may you attain all desires.’
She turned to the gods.
Thereupon the gods prospered, the Asuras were defeated.
He who, knowing thus, has the high altar piled up, and he who, knowing thus, piles it up, prospers in himself, and his rival is defeated.
Behind, it is ten steps across; on both sides, ten steps facing east; unmeasured in front, equal to the Virāj.
Whatever possessions the Asuras had, that the gods found through the altar.
That is the nature of the altar (vedi).
Whatever was to be found, [they found] through the high altar (uttaravedi).
That is the nature of the high altar.
He who, knowing thus, makes the altar and piles up the high altar, finds both the possessions and what is to be found of his rival.
Prajāpati’s nose indeed deteriorated.
It became the high altar.
Prajāpati is the sacrifice.
When he piles up the high altar,
he places Prajāpati's nose on the front.
Four indeed are its names: Nose, Kaśāri, Lioness, High Altar.
‘You are Taptāyanī (entering into heat),’ [he says].
For into heat she went to them.
‘You are Vittāyanī (entering into finding),’ [he says].
For into finding she went to them.
‘Protect me who am afflicted,’ [he says].
For she protected them when afflicted.
‘Protect him who is distressed,’ [he says].
For she protected them when distressed.
‘O Agni Aṅgiras, who are on this earth, who are on the second, who are on the third,’ [he says].
Whatever of it is attached to these worlds, whatever is hidden, he wins that.
‘Agni found [the moisture] named Nabhas,’ [he says].
Whatever lovely wealth belongs to Agni, that is Nabhas.
With that he entered this earth knee-deep beneath.
Therefore knee-deep it is to be dug,
for the finding of that very lovely wealth.
‘You are a lioness, you are a female buffalo,’ [he says].

For, having assumed the form of a lioness as it were, the form of a female buffalo as it were, she stood between [them].
'Spread out for the gods,' [he says];
he indeed spreads her out.
'Be fit for the gods,' [he says];
he indeed makes her fit.
'Purify yourself for the gods,' [he says];
he indeed purifies her.
'Adorn yourself for the gods,' [he says];
he indeed adorns her.
'May the shining, great [sun] drink the sweet soma-juice,' with this he sets the borders in order.
The high altar is indeed the vessel of the gods.
With the vessel of the gods he satisfies the deities.
Moreover, he presents the vessel of the gods to the deities.
The hyenas indeed ate the Yatis.
Being devoured and being touched, they stepped up to the high altar.
They [the hyenas] could not overpower them.
One of them smiled;
then they overpowered them.
Tearing them out one by one, they ate them.
Therefore, one should not be one who laughs in vain.
When he sweeps away [loose earth],
whatever of it was touched and unholy, that he sweeps away.
He sprinkles [it].
As great as the high altar was, so great indeed was this earth.
All around it, the Rakṣases trembled.
Having driven them away, the gods set [guards] around it with these deities,
when he sprinkles.
These directions indeed have these deities.
Having driven away the Rakṣases, he places himself all around with these deities,
for protection.
In that he besprinkles [it], in that way the oblation reaches her before Agni.
Then she said that: 'May the oblation reach me before Agni, then through me may you attain all desires.'
Then at that time the Asuras were their rivals.
They desired: 'May we conquer the rivals.'
'You are a lioness, conqueror of rivals, svāhā,' [he says];
thereby they conquered the rivals.
They desired: 'May we find cattle.'
'You are a lioness, winner of wealth and prosperity, svāhā,' [he says];
thereby they found cattle.
They desired: 'May we find offspring.'
'You are a lioness, winner of good offspring, svāhā,' [he says];
thereby they found offspring.
They desired: 'May we become the Ādityas.'
'You are a lioness, winner of the Ādityas, svāhā,' [he says];
thereby they became the Ādityas.

Therefore these creatures are Ādityas.
They desired: 'May we be worthy of sacrifice.'
'You are a lioness; bring the gods for the sacrificer who longs for the gods, svāhā,' [he says];
thereby they became worthy of sacrifice.
They desired: 'May we go to the heavenly world.'
'To the beings, for you,' [he says].
The gods are indeed the beings.
Thereby they went to the heavenly world.
He for whom, knowing thus, the high altar is besprinkled, and he who, knowing thus, besprinkles [it], attains through it all desires.
These worlds indeed were unsupported.
They trembled.
The gods supported them with these sacrificial formulas,
in that he lays down the enclosing sticks with these [formulas],
for the supporting of these worlds.
Agni indeed fled from the gods.
The first [night] that he stayed away, he lived among the beasts, between the horns of a ram.
Therefore there is a tuft of wool.
The second [night], among the trees in the deodar tree.
Therefore there is deodar wood.
The third [night], among the plants in fragrant reed-grass.
Therefore there is fragrant reed-grass.
When these materials are [brought],
whatever of him clung there, whatever was deposited, that he brings together with these.
He, turning back again, shook his body.
Whatever flesh of his there was, that became bdellium;
what was bone, that was deodar wood;
what was hair, that was fragrant reed-grass.
When these materials are [brought],
whatever of him clung there, whatever was deposited, that he brings together with these,
for the wholeness of Agni.
'You are the nest of Agni, you are the earth of Agni,' [he says];
for this is like a nest as it were, like earth as it were.
'The sacrifice has been established,' [he says],
for the establishment of the sacrifice.

25.7.s: catvāro vai devānāṃ hotāra āsan bhūpatir bhuvanapatir bhūtānāṃ patir bhūtas teṣāṃ trayo hotreṇa prāmīyanta | atho yad bhūta udaśiṣyata sa pramayād abibhet sa nyalayata sa samudraṃ prāviśat sa yat samudre bhasmākuruta sa eṣa kardamas taṃ matsyaḥ prābravīt tam aśapad abhigantā tvā hatād iti tasmān matsyam abhigantā hanti śapto hi sa tata uddrutya naḍaṃ prāviśat tasmān naḍo dagdhaḥ krūra iva varvaras tam aśvaś śveto 'vamṛśann anvavindat taṃ pratyauṣat tasmāt sa pratyuṣṭamukhas so 'krandat sā yā vāg āsīt sa suślokaś śakunir abhavat tasmād yaṃ sa naṣṭaiṣam abhyavakrandati vindaty evā taṃ devā anuvidyānayann idaṃ no hotā bhaviṣyasīti sa pramayād abibhet taṃ bhrātaraḥ pramītā abruvan vayaṃ ta ito varma bhaviṣyāmo deveṣu no bhāgadheyam iccheti te 'bruvan yat kiṃca havirbhūtaṃ bahiṣparidhi skandāt tad eṣāṃ bhāgadheyam iti | ete vāva te paridhayas | yadi havirbhūtaṃ bahiṣparidhi skanded bhūpataye svāhā bhuvanapataye svāhā bhūtānāṃ pataye svāhety anumantrayeta | ete vai devās skannabhāgās | ya eva devās skannabhāgās tān enad gamayati yajño vā eteṣāṃ madhyamo yajamāno dakṣiṇārdhyo bhrātṛvya uttarārdhyas sthaviṣṭhaṃ madhyamaṃ kuryād varṣiṣṭhaṃ dakṣiṇārdhyaṃ kradhiṣṭham uttarārdhyam | sthaviṣṭhaṃ prathamaṃ paridadhāti prathamo hi yajñas | varṣiṣṭhaṃ dakṣiṇārdhyam | yathā yajamāno dakṣiṇato yajñam upasīdaty evaṃ tat paścevottarārdhyam | paśceva hi bhrātṛvyas | yajñenaivaitad yajamānaṃ pratarām karoti yajñena bhrātṛvyam apanudate | aktvā dakṣiṇārdhye praharati mukhata eva yajamānaṃ prīṇāti | atho havirbhūtam evainaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati | upavapaty uttarārdhyam | bhrātṛvyam eva tad upavapati | atha ha smāhāryalaḥ kāhoḍiḥ kim u sa yajeta yo yajñasya skannena na vasīyān iva syād iti yatra skandet tad apo ninīya bhūpataye svāheti prāk prādeśena mimīta bhuvanapataye svāheti dakṣiṇā bhūtānāṃ pataye svāheti pratyak | janaṃ vā etad yajñasyaiti yat skandati | iyaṃ vāva janas | yo vā imām eti na sa punar āgacchanti janam evaitasya yajñasya yāṃ kāmayata āśiṣaṃ tām avarunddhe | diśo mimīte diśo vai yajñasya skannasyāśīr gacchati digbhya eva yajñasyāśiṣam avarunddhe prādeśena mimīte | etāvad vai puruṣe vīryaṃ yāvad asya prāṇā abhi yāvad evāsmin vīryaṃ tenainat saṃbharati | apo ninayati mriyate vā etad yajñasya yat skandati | adbhis tāntam abhiṣiñcanti | āpas sarvā devatās | devatā evainat praveśayati yadi prātassavane skanded devāñ janam agan yajñas tasya yajñasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgamyā ity anumantrayeta yadi madhyandine 'pa oṣadhīr janam agan yajñas tasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgamyā ity anumantrayeta yadi tṛtīyasavane pitṝñ janam agan yajñas tasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgamyā ity anumantrayeta yadi naktaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī janam agan yajñas tasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgamyā ity anumantrayeta yadi tirohnyeṣu gandharvāñ janam agan yajñas tasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgamyā ity anumantrayeta | etā vai devatā yajñasya skannasyāśīr gacchati | etā eva devatā yathādevataṃ pratyupasṛtya yāṃ kāmayate yajñasyāśiṣaṃ tām avarunddhe yasyaivaṃ viduṣo yajñasya skannam anumantrayante yaś caivaṃ vidvān anumantrayate vasīyān bhavati |
25.7.d: चत्वारो वै देवानां होतार आसन् भूपतिर् भुवनपतिर् भूतानां पतिर् भूतस् तेषां त्रयो होत्रेण प्रामीयन्त । अथो यद् भूत उदशिष्यत स प्रमयाद् अबिभेत् स न्यलयत स समुद्रं प्राविशत् स यत् समुद्रे भस्माकुरुत स एष कर्दमस् तं मत्स्यः प्राब्रवीत् तम् अशपद् अभिगन्ता त्वा हताद् इति तस्मान् मत्स्यम् अभिगन्ता हन्ति शप्तो हि स तत उद्द्रुत्य नडं प्राविशत् तस्मान् नडो दग्धः क्रूर इव वर्वरस् तम् अश्वश् श्वेतो ऽवमृशन्न् अन्वविन्दत् तं प्रत्यौषत् तस्मात् स प्रत्युष्टमुखस् सो ऽक्रन्दत् सा या वाग् आसीत् स सुश्लोकश् शकुनिर् अभवत् तस्माद् यं स नष्टैषम् अभ्यवक्रन्दति विन्दत्य् एवा तं देवा अनुविद्यानयन्न् इदं नो होता भविष्यसीति स प्रमयाद् अबिभेत् तं भ्रातरः प्रमीता अब्रुवन् वयं त इतो वर्म भविष्यामो देवेषु नो भागधेयम् इच्छेति ते ऽब्रुवन् यत् किंच हविर्भूतं बहिष्परिधि स्कन्दात् तद् एषां भागधेयम् इति । एते वाव ते परिधयस् । यदि हविर्भूतं बहिष्परिधि स्कन्देद् भूपतये स्वाहा भुवनपतये स्वाहा भूतानां पतये स्वाहेत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत । एते वै देवास् स्कन्नभागास् । य एव देवास् स्कन्नभागास् तान् एनद् गमयति यज्ञो वा एतेषां मध्यमो यजमानो दक्षिणार्ध्यो भ्रातृव्य उत्तरार्ध्यस् स्थविष्ठं मध्यमं कुर्याद् वर्षिष्ठं दक्षिणार्ध्यं क्रधिष्ठम् उत्तरार्ध्यम् । स्थविष्ठं प्रथमं परिदधाति प्रथमो हि यज्ञस् । वर्षिष्ठं दक्षिणार्ध्यम् । यथा यजमानो दक्षिणतो यज्ञम् उपसीदत्य् एवं तत् पश्चेवोत्तरार्ध्यम् । पश्चेव हि भ्रातृव्यस् । यज्ञेनैवैतद् यजमानं प्रतराम् करोति यज्ञेन भ्रातृव्यम् अपनुदते । अक्त्वा दक्षिणार्ध्ये प्रहरति मुखत एव यजमानं प्रीणाति । अथो हविर्भूतम् एवैनं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति । उपवपत्य् उत्तरार्ध्यम् । भ्रातृव्यम् एव तद् उपवपति । अथ ह स्माहार्यलः काहोडिः किम् उ स यजेत यो यज्ञस्य स्कन्नेन न वसीयान् इव स्याद् इति यत्र स्कन्देत् तद् अपो निनीय भूपतये स्वाहेति प्राक् प्रादेशेन मिमीत भुवनपतये स्वाहेति दक्षिणा भूतानां पतये स्वाहेति प्रत्यक् । जनं वा एतद् यज्ञस्यैति यत् स्कन्दति । इयं वाव जनस् । यो वा इमाम् एति न स पुनर् आगच्छन्ति जनम् एवैतस्य यज्ञस्य यां कामयत आशिषं ताम् अवरुन्द्धे । दिशो मिमीते दिशो वै यज्ञस्य स्कन्नस्याशीर् गच्छति दिग्भ्य एव यज्ञस्याशिषम् अवरुन्द्धे प्रादेशेन मिमीते । एतावद् वै पुरुषे वीर्यं यावद् अस्य प्राणा अभि यावद् एवास्मिन् वीर्यं तेनैनत् संभरति । अपो निनयति म्रियते वा एतद् यज्ञस्य यत् स्कन्दति । अद्भिस् तान्तम् अभिषिञ्चन्ति । आपस् सर्वा देवतास् । देवता एवैनत् प्रवेशयति यदि प्रातस्सवने स्कन्देद् देवाञ् जनम् अगन् यज्ञस् तस्य यज्ञस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागम्या इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत यदि मध्यन्दिने ऽप ओषधीर् जनम् अगन् यज्ञस् तस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागम्या इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत यदि तृतीयसवने पितॄञ् जनम् अगन् यज्ञस् तस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागम्या इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत यदि नक्तं द्यावापृथिवी जनम् अगन् यज्ञस् तस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागम्या इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत यदि तिरोह्न्येषु गन्धर्वाञ् जनम् अगन् यज्ञस् तस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागम्या इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयेत । एता वै देवता यज्ञस्य स्कन्नस्याशीर् गच्छति । एता एव देवता यथादेवतं प्रत्युपसृत्य यां कामयते यज्ञस्याशिषं ताम् अवरुन्द्धे यस्यैवं विदुषो यज्ञस्य स्कन्नम् अनुमन्त्रयन्ते यश् चैवं विद्वान् अनुमन्त्रयते वसीयान् भवति ।
25.7.m:
The gods indeed had four Hotṛs: Bhūpati, Bhuvanapati, Bhūtānām Pati, and Bhūta.
Three of them perished through the office of Hotṛ.
Now, because Bhūta was left over, he feared death.
He hid himself.
He entered the sea.
The ashes that he made in the sea became this mud.
A fish pointed him out.
He cursed it: 'May a hunter strike you!'
Therefore a hunter strikes a fish,
for it was cursed.
Running up from there, he entered a reed.
Therefore a burnt reed is harsh and crude, as it were.
A white horse found him out by touching.
He scorched its face.
Therefore it has a scorched mouth.
He cried out.
The voice that it was became the bird of good omen.
Therefore, whichever seeker of what is lost it cries out towards, he indeed finds [it].
The gods, having found him, led him back: 'You shall be our Hotṛ here.'
He feared death.
His dead brothers said to him: 'We will be your shield from this side; seek a share for us among the gods.'
They said: 'Whatever, having become an oblation, spills outside the enclosing-sticks, that shall be their share.'
These enclosing-sticks are indeed they.
If, having become an oblation, it should spill outside the enclosing-sticks, he should accompany it with the formula: 'To Bhūpati, svāhā! To Bhuvanapati, svāhā! To Bhūtānām Pati, svāhā!'
These gods are indeed those whose share is what is spilt.
He causes it to reach those very gods whose share is what is spilt.
The middle one of these is the sacrifice, the southern one is the sacrificer, the northern one is the rival.
He should make the middle one thickest, the southern one highest, the northern one shortest.
He lays down the thickest first,
for the sacrifice is first;
the highest on the south,
just as the sacrificer sits near the sacrifice on the south, so is that;
the northern one behind, as it were,
for the rival is behind, as it were.
Thereby he makes the sacrificer advance through the sacrifice, and thrusts away the rival through the sacrifice.
Having anointed [the fuel-stick], he throws it on the southern one;
he pleases the sacrificer right from the mouth.
Moreover, having become an oblation, he causes him to reach the heavenly world.
He piles earth upon the northern one;
he thereby piles earth upon the rival.
Now Āryala Kāhoḍi used to say:
'Why indeed should he sacrifice who would not become wealthier, as it were, through what is spilt of the sacrifice?'
Where it spills, having poured water there, he should measure out with a span towards the east: 'To Bhūpati, svāhā!'; towards the south: 'To Bhuvanapati, svāhā!'; towards the west: 'To Bhūtānām Pati, svāhā!'
What spills indeed goes to the foreign people of the sacrifice.
This [earth] is indeed the foreign people.
Whoever goes to this [foreign people], they do not return.
Whatever blessing he desires from this sacrifice, that he secures from the foreign people.
He measures the directions.
The blessing of what is spilt of the sacrifice goes indeed to the directions.
He secures the blessing of the sacrifice from the directions.
He measures with a span.
So much indeed is the virility in man as his vital breaths reach.
With as much virility as is in him, with that he collects it.
He pours down water.
That which spills of the sacrifice dies, as it were.
They sprinkle with water one who is exhausted.
Water is all the deities.
He causes it to enter the deities.
If it should spill at the morning pressing, he should accompany it with the formula: 'The sacrifice has gone to the gods, to the foreign people; of that sacrifice, sacrificed, enjoyed, may the wealth come here.'
If at midday, he should accompany it with the formula: 'The sacrifice has gone to the waters, to the plants, to the foreign people; of that [sacrifice], sacrificed, enjoyed, may the wealth come here.'
If at the third pressing, he should accompany it with the formula: 'The sacrifice has gone to the fathers, to the foreign people; of that sacrifice, sacrificed, enjoyed, may the wealth come here.'
If at night, he should accompany it with the formula: 'The sacrifice has gone to heaven and earth, to the foreign people; of that sacrifice, sacrificed, enjoyed, may the wealth come here.'
If during the overnight [rites], he should accompany it with the formula: 'The sacrifice has gone to the Gandharvas, to the foreign people; of that sacrifice, sacrificed, enjoyed, may the wealth come here.'
To these deities indeed goes the blessing of what is spilt of the sacrifice.
Having approached these very deities, deity by deity, he secures whatever blessing of the sacrifice he desires.
He for whose sacrifice, knowing thus, they accompany what is spilt, and he who, knowing thus, accompanies it, becomes wealthier.

25.8.s: havirdhāne praṇenekti medhye evaine yajñiye karoti granthīn vicṛtanti devagranthīn eva granthiṣyanto manuṣyagranthīn vicṛtanti havir vai havirdhāne stīrṇe barhiṣi havir āsādayanti tasmāt stīrṇe barhiṣi havirdhāne pravartayanti patny upānakti patnyā evaiṣa yajñasyānvārambhas | atho mithunam eva yajñamukhe dadhāti prajananāya triḥ prācīnam upānakti | asaṃkhyātaṃ hi tiraścīnaṃ manuṣyā upāñjanti vyāvṛttyai yajuṣopānakti | ayajuṣā hi manuṣyā upāñjanti vyāvṛttyai dakṣiṇata upānakti dakṣiṇato hy ete udīcī manuṣyalokam upāvartete mānuṣam evainayor uttaraṃ karoti | yad uttarād upāñjyān nānyataraṃ cana lokam upāvarteyātām | svargāya vā ete lokāya pravartete yad dhavirdhāne yuñjate mana iti sāvitryā juhoti savitṛprasūte evaine svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati havir vai havirdhāne na havir anabhighṛtaṃ medham aśnute yad abhyanakti | abhy evaine ghārayati medhyatvāya śuṣko vā eṣa nirṛtigṛhīto yad akṣo nabhyābhyām ubhayato baddha upadhibhyāṃ saṃdaṣṭas | yad upānakti medhyam evainaṃ yajñiyaṃ karoti ghoṣo vai nāmāsura āsīt sa vanaspatīn prāviśat taṃ devā gṛhītvobhayato 'badhnan yat kṣveded asuryā vāg yajñam avavaded rakṣāṃsi yajñam anvavetya hanyur anugṛhṇanto yanti rakṣasām ananvavāyāya vartmanā vai yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsy anvavetya jighāṃsanti vaiṣṇavyā vartmañ juhoti viṣṇur vai yajñas | viṣṇunaiva yajñād rakṣāṃsy apahanti vyṛddhā vā eṣāhutir yām anagnau juhoti yad dhiraṇyam upāsya juhoti | agnimaty eva juhoti samṛddhyai svargaṃ vā ete lokaṃ preto yad dhavirdhāne gāyatryā dakṣiṇasya vartmañ juhoti | asyām evaine ākramayati triṣṭubhottarasya | antarikṣa evaine ākramayati | āhavanīyaṃ gamayati svargam evaine lokaṃ gamayati svargo hi loka āhavanīyas trīn purastāt prakramān ucchiṃṣati traya ime lokās | imān evāsmai lokān ucchiṃṣati | divo vā viṣṇa uta vā pṛthivyā iti dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya methīm upaminoti viṣṇur vai yajñas | mukhata eva yajñasyāśiṣam avarunddhe tāṃ paruṣiparuṣy āśāsāna eti viṣṇor nu kaṃ vīryāṇi pravocam ity uttarasya vaiṣṇavaṃ vai havirdhānam | svayaivainad devatayā samardhayati viṣṇoḥ pṛṣṭham asīti cchadir upariṣṭād adhinidadhāti | idam eva tena karoti yad idam uttarārdhaṃ śīrṣṇas | viṣṇo rarāṭam asīti purastāt | rarāṭam eva tena karoti viṣṇoś śnaptre stha ity abhitas | śnaptre eva tena karoti | tiryañcaṃ purastād vaṃśaṃ viṣīvyanti tasmāt tiraścī puruṣasya bhruvau viṣṇos syūr asi viṣṇor dhruvo 'sīti vaiṣṇavaṃ vai havirdhānam | svayaiva devatayā sīvyati svayā devatayā granthiṃ grathnāti yaṃ prathamaṃ granthiṃ grathnīyāt taṃ prathamaṃ vicṛtet | ātmano gopīthāya yad anyaṃ pūrvaṃ vicṛted amehenādhvaryuḥ pramīyeta | upariṣṭāc chamyās saṃnahyanti paścād upaminvanti | adhastād dhi manuṣyā yuñjanti purastād upaminvanti vyāvṛttyai | śiro vā etad yajñasya yad dhavirdhānam | purastād varṣīyo bhavati paścāt kradhīyas tasmāt purastāt puruṣasya śiro varṣīyaḥ paścāt kradhīyas | vaiṣṇavam asi viṣṇave tveti saṃmitam abhimantrayate vaiṣṇavaṃ vai havirdhānam | svayaivainad devatayā samardhayati pra tad viṣṇus stavate vīryeṇeti trīn prakramān yajamānaṃ prāñcaṃ prakramayati viṣṇum evainaṃ bhūtam imāṃl lokān gamayati |
25.8.d: हविर्धाने प्रणेनेक्ति मेध्ये एवैने यज्ञिये करोति ग्रन्थीन् विचृतन्ति देवग्रन्थीन् एव ग्रन्थिष्यन्तो मनुष्यग्रन्थीन् विचृतन्ति हविर् वै हविर्धाने स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि हविर् आसादयन्ति तस्मात् स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि हविर्धाने प्रवर्तयन्ति पत्न्य् उपानक्ति पत्न्या एवैष यज्ञस्यान्वारम्भस् । अथो मिथुनम् एव यज्ञमुखे दधाति प्रजननाय त्रिः प्राचीनम् उपानक्ति । असंख्यातं हि तिरश्चीनं मनुष्या उपाञ्जन्ति व्यावृत्त्यै यजुषोपानक्ति । अयजुषा हि मनुष्या उपाञ्जन्ति व्यावृत्त्यै दक्षिणत उपानक्ति दक्षिणतो ह्य् एते उदीची मनुष्यलोकम् उपावर्तेते मानुषम् एवैनयोर् उत्तरं करोति । यद् उत्तराद् उपाञ्ज्यान् नान्यतरं चन लोकम् उपावर्तेयाताम् । स्वर्गाय वा एते लोकाय प्रवर्तेते यद् धविर्धाने युञ्जते मन इति सावित्र्या जुहोति सवितृप्रसूते एवैने स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति हविर् वै हविर्धाने न हविर् अनभिघृतं मेधम् अश्नुते यद् अभ्यनक्ति । अभ्य् एवैने घारयति मेध्यत्वाय शुष्को वा एष निरृतिगृहीतो यद् अक्षो नभ्याभ्याम् उभयतो बद्ध उपधिभ्यां संदष्टस् । यद् उपानक्ति मेध्यम् एवैनं यज्ञियं करोति घोषो वै नामासुर आसीत् स वनस्पतीन् प्राविशत् तं देवा गृहीत्वोभयतो ऽबध्नन् यत् क्ष्वेदेद् असुर्या वाग् यज्ञम् अववदेद् रक्षांसि यज्ञम् अन्ववेत्य हन्युर् अनुगृह्णन्तो यन्ति रक्षसाम् अनन्ववायाय वर्त्मना वै यज्ञं रक्षांस्य् अन्ववेत्य जिघांसन्ति वैष्णव्या वर्त्मञ् जुहोति विष्णुर् वै यज्ञस् । विष्णुनैव यज्ञाद् रक्षांस्य् अपहन्ति व्यृद्धा वा एषाहुतिर् याम् अनग्नौ जुहोति यद् धिरण्यम् उपास्य जुहोति । अग्निमत्य् एव जुहोति समृद्ध्यै स्वर्गं वा एते लोकं प्रेतो यद् धविर्धाने गायत्र्या दक्षिणस्य वर्त्मञ् जुहोति । अस्याम् एवैने आक्रमयति त्रिष्टुभोत्तरस्य । अन्तरिक्ष एवैने आक्रमयति । आहवनीयं गमयति स्वर्गम् एवैने लोकं गमयति स्वर्गो हि लोक आहवनीयस् त्रीन् पुरस्तात् प्रक्रमान् उच्छिंषति त्रय इमे लोकास् । इमान् एवास्मै लोकान् उच्छिंषति । दिवो वा विष्ण उत वा पृथिव्या इति दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य मेथीम् उपमिनोति विष्णुर् वै यज्ञस् । मुखत एव यज्ञस्याशिषम् अवरुन्द्धे तां परुषिपरुष्य् आशासान एति विष्णोर् नु कं वीर्याणि प्रवोचम् इत्य् उत्तरस्य वैष्णवं वै हविर्धानम् । स्वयैवैनद् देवतया समर्धयति विष्णोः पृष्ठम् असीति च्छदिर् उपरिष्टाद् अधिनिदधाति । इदम् एव तेन करोति यद् इदम् उत्तरार्धं शीर्ष्णस् । विष्णो रराटम् असीति पुरस्तात् । रराटम् एव तेन करोति विष्णोश् श्नप्त्रे स्थ इत्य् अभितस् । श्नप्त्रे एव तेन करोति । तिर्यञ्चं पुरस्ताद् वंशं विषीव्यन्ति तस्मात् तिरश्ची पुरुषस्य भ्रुवौ विष्णोस् स्यूर् असि विष्णोर् ध्रुवो ऽसीति वैष्णवं वै हविर्धानम् । स्वयैव देवतया सीव्यति स्वया देवतया ग्रन्थिं ग्रथ्नाति यं प्रथमं ग्रन्थिं ग्रथ्नीयात् तं प्रथमं विचृतेत् । आत्मनो गोपीथाय यद् अन्यं पूर्वं विचृतेद् अमेहेनाध्वर्युः प्रमीयेत । उपरिष्टाच् छम्यास् संनह्यन्ति पश्चाद् उपमिन्वन्ति । अधस्ताद् धि मनुष्या युञ्जन्ति पुरस्ताद् उपमिन्वन्ति व्यावृत्त्यै । शिरो वा एतद् यज्ञस्य यद् धविर्धानम् । पुरस्ताद् वर्षीयो भवति पश्चात् क्रधीयस् तस्मात् पुरस्तात् पुरुषस्य शिरो वर्षीयः पश्चात् क्रधीयस् । वैष्णवम् असि विष्णवे त्वेति संमितम् अभिमन्त्रयते वैष्णवं वै हविर्धानम् । स्वयैवैनद् देवतया समर्धयति प्र तद् विष्णुस् स्तवते वीर्येणेति त्रीन् प्रक्रमान् यजमानं प्राञ्चं प्रक्रमयति विष्णुम् एवैनं भूतम् इमांल् लोकान् गमयति ।
25.8.m:
He cleans the two oblation-carts.
He thereby makes them fit for offering, worthy of sacrifice.
They untie the knots.
Intending to tie the knots of the gods, they untie the knots of men.
The oblation indeed is the two oblation-carts.
They place the oblation on the strewn sacrificial grass;
therefore, they roll forward the two oblation-carts on the strewn sacrificial grass.
The wife anoints [them].
This is indeed the wife's holding on to the sacrifice.
Moreover, he places a pair at the opening of the sacrifice,
for procreation.
Three times she anoints eastward;
for men anoint crosswise, innumerably,
for distinction.
She anoints with a Yajus formula;
for men anoint without a Yajus formula,
for distinction.
She anoints from the south;
for these two [carts], [facing] northwards, turn toward the world of men from the south.
He thereby makes their northern [part] human.
If she were to anoint from the north, they would not turn toward either world.
The two oblation-carts indeed roll forward to the heavenly world.
With a verse addressed to Savitṛ, 'They yoke the mind,' he offers.
Impelled by Savitṛ, he causes them to go to the heavenly world.
The oblation indeed is the two oblation-carts.
An oblation that is not basted with ghee does not attain fitness for offering.
In that he anoints [them],
he indeed besprinkles them with ghee,
for fitness for offering.
Dried up indeed and seized by Nirṛti is the axle, bound on both sides by the two navels and bitten by the two spokes.
In that he anoints [it],
he indeed makes it fit for offering, worthy of sacrifice.
There was an Asura named Ghoṣa.
He entered the trees.
The gods seized him and bound him on both sides.
If it were to creak, the Asuric voice would speak against the sacrifice, [and] the Rakṣases, following into the sacrifice, would slay [it].
They go holding [it] firmly,
so that the Rakṣases do not follow.
The Rakṣases, following by the track, desire to slay the sacrifice.
With a verse to Viṣṇu he offers in the track.
Viṣṇu indeed is the sacrifice.
With Viṣṇu he smites away the Rakṣases from the sacrifice.
Deprived indeed is that oblation which one offers not in fire.
In that he offers having thrown gold [into the track],
he offers as if in fire,
for success.
These two oblation-carts indeed go to the heavenly world.
With a Gāyatrī verse he offers in the track of the southern [cart];
he causes them to step upon this [earth].
With a Triṣṭubh verse [in the track] of the northern [cart];
he causes them to step into the intermediate space.
He causes them to go to the Āhavanīya fire;
he causes them to go to the heavenly world,
for the Āhavanīya is the heavenly world.
He leaves three steps in front.
Three are these worlds;
he leaves these worlds for him.
'From heaven, O Viṣṇu, or from earth,' with this he fastens the peg of the southern oblation-cart.
Viṣṇu indeed is the sacrifice;
he secures the blessing of the sacrifice right from the mouth.
He goes praying at joint after joint.
'Now I will proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu,' [with this he fastens the peg] of the northern [cart].
To Viṣṇu indeed belongs the oblation-cart;
with its own deity he makes it prosper.
'You are the back of Viṣṇu,' with this he puts the roof on above.
By that he makes this, which is the upper half of the head.
'You are the forehead of Viṣṇu,' [with this he places it] in front;
by that he makes the forehead.
'You two are the corners of Viṣṇu's mouth,' [with this he places two mats] on both sides;
by that he makes the corners of the mouth.
They sew across the crossbeam in front;
therefore a man's two eyebrows are transverse.
'You are the stitch of Viṣṇu; you are the firm point of Viṣṇu,' [he says].
To Viṣṇu indeed belongs the oblation-cart;
with its own deity he sews [it],
with its own deity he ties the knot.
Whichever knot he ties first, that he should untie first,
for the protection of himself.
If he were to untie another first, the Adhvaryu would die of retention of urine.
They bind the yoke-pins above; they fasten the pegs behind;
for men yoke below and fasten pegs in front,
for distinction.
The oblation-cart is indeed the head of the sacrifice.
In front it is broader, behind it is shorter;
therefore, a man's head is broader in front, shorter behind.
'You belong to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu you,' with this he addresses it when properly measured.
To Viṣṇu indeed belongs the oblation-cart;
with its own deity he makes it prosper.
'For this Viṣṇu is praised for his heroism,' with this he causes the sacrificer to take three strides forward;
having become Viṣṇu, he causes him to go to these worlds.

The head of the sacrifice indeed is the oblation-cart shed, the vital breaths are the sound-holes.
He draws a line around beneath the southern oblation-cart.
This indeed is the earlier of the two.
He places the vital breaths right at the mouth of the sacrifice.
Therefore the vital breaths are at the mouth.
He draws a line around four [of them];
for the vital breaths are four.
He draws lines around apart from one another at a span's distance each.
For by so much these vital breaths correspond to one another. Not breaking [into each other], they dig,
so that the vital breaths do not break into one another.
If he were to break them into one another, he would break the vital breaths into one another; [the sacrificer] would perish.
Beyond, they pierce them together into one.
Therefore the vital breaths beyond are pierced together into one.
'At the impulse of the god Savitṛ [I take you],' [saying this] he takes the spade.
Impelled by Savitṛ, he takes it with the deities.
'Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas,' [he says].
The rival indeed is the Rakṣas.
He cuts off the neck of the rival.
'Here I cut off the neck of him who, being our equal or not our equal, plots evil against us,' [he says].
The sound-holes indeed are the vital breaths.
He excludes the rival from the vital breaths; he quickly perishes.
'You are great, possessing a great pressing-stone; speak great speech unto Indra,' [he says].
For he speaks great speech unto Indra.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu,' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides it fully with its own deity.
The gods and the Asuras indeed practiced sorcery against each other.
Those Asuras buried charms in the vital breaths of the gods.
They found them at an arm's depth.
Therefore [holes] of an arm's depth are to be dug,
for the finding of the vital breaths.
'Here I cast out those charms which our equal, which [one] not our equal buried,' [he says].
Whatever was cursed against him here, whatever sorcery was practiced against him, having found that, he casts it out.
Therefore these [holes] are healing.
Therefore they touch [them] for one who is ill.
'You are sovereign, you are self-ruler,' [he says];
he attains sovereignty through these.
'Kept down by the Gāyatrī metre is he whom we hate, by the Triṣṭubh, by the Jagatī,' [he says].
So many indeed are the metres.
By means of the metres he keeps down the rival.
'What good is here, may that be with both of us,' [he says];
he utters a blessing.
'Cast away is the charm, kept down is the malicious one,' [he says];
[it is] according to the sacrificial formula.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I sprinkle [you],' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides them fully with their own deity.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I pour down [water],' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
Moreover, whatever harsh [wound] they cause to them while digging, that he pacifies.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides them fully with their own deity.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I strew down [grass],' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides them fully with their own deity.
He pours down [water] and strews down [grass].
Therefore the vital breaths are hairy on the inside and watery.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I sprinkle the two,' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides the two fully with their own deity.
Unfit for sacrifice are these two, trimmed with an axe.
The waters are fit for offering, worthy of sacrifice.
When he sprinkles with waters,
he makes them fit for offering, worthy of sacrifice.
The two jaws of the sacrifice indeed are the two pressing-boards.
They are not pierced through.
Therefore the two jaws are not pierced through.
Narrower in front, broader behind [they are];
for even so are the two jaws.
There is a space of two finger-breadths between the two pressing-boards.
Therefore this [tongue] between the two jaws is like a tongue-strap.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I place the two down,' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides the two fully with their own deity.
'Slaying the Rakṣases, slaying the charms, belonging to Viṣṇu, I bank the two around,' [he says],
for the warding off of the Rakṣases.
As for [saying], 'belonging to Viṣṇu':
the sacrifice indeed is Viṣṇu;
he provides the two fully with their own deity.
He banks [them] around.
Therefore the two jaws are not naked, not exposed, [being covered] with gums, lips, corners of the mouth, and beards.
The head of the sacrifice indeed is the oblation-cart shed, the vital breaths are the sound-holes, the two jaws are the two pressing-boards, the teeth are the pressing-stones, the tongue is the pressing-skin, the skull is the Droṇakalaśa trough.
The sacrifice is Prajāpati.
From the mouth of Prajāpati here they drink out the Soma.
Therefore the Soma-dregs are as if chewed, as if masticated.
For thus it is masticated with the teeth.
He who knows the Virāj as milkable at the opening of the sacrifice milks her.
This [earth] indeed is the Virāj.
Her udder is the two pressing-boards, her teats are the sound-holes, her calves are the pressing-stones, her skin is the pressing-skin.
The priests milk [her].
He who thus knows the Virāj as milkable at the opening of the sacrifice milks her.

25.9.s: śiro vā etad yajñasya yad dhavirdhānaṃ prāṇā uparavās | dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyādhastāt parilikhati | etad vā etayoḥ pūrvam | mukhata eva yajñasya prāṇān pratidadhāti tasmān mukhataḥ prāṇās | caturaḥ parilikhati catvāro hi prāṇāḥ prādeśaṃprādeśaṃ viparilikhati | etāvadetāvad dhīme 'bhi prāṇā asaṃbhindantaḥ khananti prāṇānām asaṃbhedāya yat saṃbhindyāt prāṇān saṃbhindyāt pramīyeta tān para ekadhā saṃtṛndanti tasmāt prāṇāḥ para ekadhā saṃtṛṇṇās | devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ity abhrim ādatte savitṛprasūta evaināṃ devatābhir ādatte | idam ahaṃ rakṣaso grīvā apikṛntāmīti bhrātṛvyo vai rakṣas | bhrātṛvyasyaiva grīvā apikṛntati | idam ahaṃ yo nas samāno yo 'samāno 'rātīyati tasya grīvā apikṛntāmīti | prāṇā vā uparavāḥ prāṇebhya eva bhrātṛvyam antareti tājak pradhanvati bṛhann asi bṛhadgrāvā bṛhatīm indrāya vācaṃ vadeti bṛhatīṃ hy eṣa indrāya vācaṃ vadati rakṣohaṇaṃ valagahanaṃ vaiṣṇavīm iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavīm iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivaināṃ devatayā samardhayati devāś ca vā asurāś ca vyabhyacaranta te 'surā devānāṃ prāṇeṣu valagān nyakhanan | tān bāhumātre 'nvavindan | tasmād bāhumātrāḥ kheyāḥ prāṇānām anuvittyai | idam ahaṃ tān valagān udvapāmi yān nas samāno yān asamāno nicakhāneti yad evāsyātra śaptaṃ yad abhicaritaṃ tad anuvidyodvapati tasmād ete bhiṣajyās tasmād āmayāvinam anumarśayanti | samrāḍ asi svarāḍ asīti sāmrājyam evaitair upaiti gāyatreṇa cchandasāvabāḍho yaṃ dviṣmas traiṣṭubhena jāgateneti | etāvanti vai chandāṃsi cchandobhir eva bhrātṛvyam avabādhate kim atra bhadraṃ tan nau saheti | āśiṣam evāśāste nirasto valago 'vabāḍho durasyur iti yathāyajus | rakṣoghno valagaghnaḥ prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavān iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavān iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivainān devatayā samardhayati rakṣoghno valagaghno 'vasiñcāmi vaiṣṇavān iti rakṣasām apahatyai | atho yad evaiṣāṃ khanantaḥ krūraṃ kurvanti tac chamayati yad vaiṣṇavān iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivainān devatayā samardhayati rakṣoghno valagaghno 'vastṛṇāmi vaiṣṇavān iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavān iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivainān devatayā samardhayati | avasiñcaty ava ca stṛṇāti tasmāt prāṇā antarato lomaśā udanvantas | rakṣohaṇau valagahanau prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavī iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavī iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivaine devatayā samardhayati | ṛkṣe vā ete taṣṭe amedhye āpo medhyā yajñiyās | yad adbhiḥ prokṣati medhye evaine yajñiye karoti hanū vā ete yajñasya yad adhiṣavaṇe avitṛṇṇe bhavatas tasmād dhanū avitṛṇṇe purastād aṃhīyasī paścād varīyasī evam eva hi hanū dvyaṅgulam antarādhiṣavaṇe bhavati tasmād iyam antarā hanū rāsnākeva rakṣohaṇau valagahanā upadadhāmi vaiṣṇavī iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavī iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivaine devatayā samardhayati rakṣohaṇau valagahanau paryūhāmi vaiṣṇavī iti rakṣasām apahatyai yad vaiṣṇavī iti yajño vai viṣṇus svayaivaine devatayā samardhayati | paryūhati tasmād dhanū anagne amuṣite barsvair oṣṭhābhyāṃ sṛkkābhyāṃ śmaśrubhis | śiro vā etad yajñasya yad dhavirdhānaṃ prāṇā uparavā hanū adhiṣavaṇe dantā grāvāṇo jihvādhiṣavaṇaṃ carma mūrdhā droṇakalaśas | yajñaḥ prajāpatis | mukhato vā idaṃ prajāpates somaṃ niṣpibanti tasmād ṛjīṣaṃ jagdham iva psātam iva | evaṃ hi dadbhiḥ psātaṃ bhavati yo virājaṃ yajñamukhe dohyāṃ veda duha enām iyaṃ vāva virāṭ tasyā etad ūdho yad adhiṣavaṇe stanā uparavā vatsā grāvāṇas tvag adhiṣavaṇaṃ carma | ṛtvijo duhanti ya evaṃ virājaṃ yajñamukhe dohyāṃ veda duha enām |
25.9.d: शिरो वा एतद् यज्ञस्य यद् धविर्धानं प्राणा उपरवास् । दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्याधस्तात् परिलिखति । एतद् वा एतयोः पूर्वम् । मुखत एव यज्ञस्य प्राणान् प्रतिदधाति तस्मान् मुखतः प्राणास् । चतुरः परिलिखति चत्वारो हि प्राणाः प्रादेशंप्रादेशं विपरिलिखति । एतावदेतावद् धीमे ऽभि प्राणा असंभिन्दन्तः खनन्ति प्राणानाम् असंभेदाय यत् संभिन्द्यात् प्राणान् संभिन्द्यात् प्रमीयेत तान् पर एकधा संतृन्दन्ति तस्मात् प्राणाः पर एकधा संतृण्णास् । देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदत्ते सवितृप्रसूत एवैनां देवताभिर् आदत्ते । इदम् अहं रक्षसो ग्रीवा अपिकृन्तामीति भ्रातृव्यो वै रक्षस् । भ्रातृव्यस्यैव ग्रीवा अपिकृन्तति । इदम् अहं यो नस् समानो यो ऽसमानो ऽरातीयति तस्य ग्रीवा अपिकृन्तामीति । प्राणा वा उपरवाः प्राणेभ्य एव भ्रातृव्यम् अन्तरेति ताजक् प्रधन्वति बृहन्न् असि बृहद्ग्रावा बृहतीम् इन्द्राय वाचं वदेति बृहतीं ह्य् एष इन्द्राय वाचं वदति रक्षोहणं वलगहनं वैष्णवीम् इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवीम् इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैनां देवतया समर्धयति देवाश् च वा असुराश् च व्यभ्यचरन्त ते ऽसुरा देवानां प्राणेषु वलगान् न्यखनन् । तान् बाहुमात्रे ऽन्वविन्दन् । तस्माद् बाहुमात्राः खेयाः प्राणानाम् अनुवित्त्यै । इदम् अहं तान् वलगान् उद्वपामि यान् नस् समानो यान् असमानो निचखानेति यद् एवास्यात्र शप्तं यद् अभिचरितं तद् अनुविद्योद्वपति तस्माद् एते भिषज्यास् तस्माद् आमयाविनम् अनुमर्शयन्ति । सम्राड् असि स्वराड् असीति साम्राज्यम् एवैतैर् उपैति गायत्रेण च्छन्दसावबाढो यं द्विष्मस् त्रैष्टुभेन जागतेनेति । एतावन्ति वै छन्दांसि च्छन्दोभिर् एव भ्रातृव्यम् अवबाधते किम् अत्र भद्रं तन् नौ सहेति । आशिषम् एवाशास्ते निरस्तो वलगो ऽवबाढो दुरस्युर् इति यथायजुस् । रक्षोघ्नो वलगघ्नः प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवान् इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवान् इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैनान् देवतया समर्धयति रक्षोघ्नो वलगघ्नो ऽवसिञ्चामि वैष्णवान् इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै । अथो यद् एवैषां खनन्तः क्रूरं कुर्वन्ति तच् छमयति यद् वैष्णवान् इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैनान् देवतया समर्धयति रक्षोघ्नो वलगघ्नो ऽवस्तृणामि वैष्णवान् इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवान् इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैनान् देवतया समर्धयति । अवसिञ्चत्य् अव च स्तृणाति तस्मात् प्राणा अन्तरतो लोमशा उदन्वन्तस् । रक्षोहणौ वलगहनौ प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवी इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवी इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैने देवतया समर्धयति । ऋक्षे वा एते तष्टे अमेध्ये आपो मेध्या यज्ञियास् । यद् अद्भिः प्रोक्षति मेध्ये एवैने यज्ञिये करोति हनू वा एते यज्ञस्य यद् अधिषवणे अवितृण्णे भवतस् तस्माद् धनू अवितृण्णे पुरस्ताद् अंहीयसी पश्चाद् वरीयसी एवम् एव हि हनू द्व्यङ्गुलम् अन्तराधिषवणे भवति तस्माद् इयम् अन्तरा हनू रास्नाकेव रक्षोहणौ वलगहना उपदधामि वैष्णवी इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवी इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैने देवतया समर्धयति रक्षोहणौ वलगहनौ पर्यूहामि वैष्णवी इति रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै यद् वैष्णवी इति यज्ञो वै विष्णुस् स्वयैवैने देवतया समर्धयति । पर्यूहति तस्माद् धनू अनग्ने अमुषिते बर्स्वैर् ओष्ठाभ्यां सृक्काभ्यां श्मश्रुभिस् । शिरो वा एतद् यज्ञस्य यद् धविर्धानं प्राणा उपरवा हनू अधिषवणे दन्ता ग्रावाणो जिह्वाधिषवणं चर्म मूर्धा द्रोणकलशस् । यज्ञः प्रजापतिस् । मुखतो वा इदं प्रजापतेस् सोमं निष्पिबन्ति तस्माद् ऋजीषं जग्धम् इव प्सातम् इव । एवं हि दद्भिः प्सातं भवति यो विराजं यज्ञमुखे दोह्यां वेद दुह एनाम् इयं वाव विराट् तस्या एतद् ऊधो यद् अधिषवणे स्तना उपरवा वत्सा ग्रावाणस् त्वग् अधिषवणं चर्म । ऋत्विजो दुहन्ति य एवं विराजं यज्ञमुखे दोह्यां वेद दुह एनाम् ।
25.9.m:
The head of the sacrifice indeed is the oblation-cart shed;
the neck is the Āgnīdhra [shed], the belly is the Sadas;
the udumbara tree is vigor.
When he erects the Audumbarī [post] in the Sadas,
he places vigor right in the middle, in the sacrificer and in [his] offspring;
therefore, vigor invigorates offspring from the middle.
For this world indeed the Audumbarī is erected; for that world, the sacrificial post.
Therefore he sprinkles the sacrificial post from here pointing away, and the Audumbarī from there pointing hither,
to hold apart these two worlds.
The udumbara tree indeed is vigor.
When he sprinkles the Audumbarī from there pointing hither,
he causes vigor to flow from there pointing hither.
He pours out vigor right into this world.
Of Prajāpati, the Udgātṛ's vigor
rests upon the Audumbarī.
He pours out vigor right into [the sacrificer's] offspring.
'At the impulse of the god Savitṛ…'—with this he takes the spade.
Impelled by Savitṛ, he takes it with the deities.
'Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas'—
the rival indeed is the Rakṣas;
he cuts off the neck of the rival.
'Let the worlds be cleansed, the seats of the Fathers'—
he cleanses it indeed.
Moreover, what cruel act they commit in digging it, that he appeases.
He pours down [water] containing barley.
Food indeed is barley, the udumbara tree is vigor;
he places vigor in food.
'I strew thee, a world that is a seat of the Fathers'—
if they were to erect it without strewn grass, it would be a pit-post.
The plants are on the northern half of this [earth]; he erects it right on the northern half of this [earth].
He has made it not a pit-post.
'Prop up the sky, fill the atmosphere, stand firm on the earth'—
he makes it firm indeed.
'May Nitāna Māruta drive thee down'—
Nitāna indeed is the mind, the vital breaths are the Mārutas;
he sets it down with its own deity.
Nitāna Māruta indeed used to erect the Audumbarī of the gods;
with him he erects it.
'By the firm law of Mitra and Varuṇa'—
by Mitra indeed these offspring are appeased, by Varuṇa held apart;
[it is] for proper ordering, for holding apart.
'Thee, winner of the priesthood, winner of the nobility'—
he utters a blessing.
'Strengthen the priesthood, strengthen the nobility'—
he strengthens for him the very blessing that has been wished.
'With ghee fill ye two heaven and earth'—
he moistens heaven and earth with ghee.
Therefore plants rustle even when unanointed.
He pours an oblation with ghee onto the Audumbarī.
Fiery energy indeed is ghee, the udumbara tree is food;
he places fiery energy in food.
He places sap throughout the trees and the plants right to the end.
'The shadow of all people art thou'—
for it is the shadow of all people;
for people crawl together [under it] from clan to clan.
He should make the roofs face towards the Audumbarī.
The divine subjects indeed are the plants;
the roofs are the plants;
the Audumbarī is the sacrificer.
He makes the subjects face towards the sacrificer.
There is a roof,
and then the inner covering;
therefore man has flesh,
and then the rib.
The belly of the sacrifice indeed is the Sadas.
They erect it crosswise;
therefore what is eaten is held in man.
If they were to erect it lengthwise, what is eaten would not be held in man.
The sacrifice is measured by man, man by the sacrifice.
In that the Sadas is perforated at both ends,
therefore man is perforated at both ends.
They sew it;
therefore man is sewn together within.
'Thou art Indra's seam, thou art Indra's knot'—
the Sadas indeed belongs to Indra;
he sews it with its own deity,
he ties the knot with its own deity.
'Thou art Indra's, for Indra thee'—he consecrates what has been measured.
The Sadas indeed belongs to Indra;
he makes it prosper with its own deity.
He should make nine roofs if it is an Agniṣṭoma,
measured by the ninefold stoma, by fiery energy;
fifteen if an Ukthya,
measured by the fifteenfold [stoma];
the fifteenfold is the thunderbolt,
measured by the thunderbolt;
seventeen if an Atirātra,
measured by the seventeenfold [stoma];
Prajāpati is seventeenfold,
measured by Prajāpati;
he should make twenty-one for one who desires a firm standing;
the twenty-onefold is the firm standing of the stomas,
for a firm standing;
moreover, for distinguishing the sacrificial rites.
The posts that are at the edges he should make shortest if he desires, 'May it rain';
for the sky is, as it were, low when about to rain.
He should make them tallest if he desires, 'May it not rain';
for the sky is, as it were, high when not about to rain.
The roofs that are southern he should make higher;
those that are southern are in the world of the sacrificer, the higher ones in the world of the rival;
he makes the sacrificer superior to his rival who does not sacrifice;
for the sacrificer is superior to the non-sacrificer.
Thus the twenty-fifth Sthānaka, named Iṣusthānaka, in the Madhyamikā of the Caraka recension of the glorious Kāṭhaka Yajurveda, is complete.

25.10.s: śiro vā etad yajñasya yad dhavirdhānam | grīvā āgnīdhram udaraṃ sadas | ūrg udumbaras | yat sadasy audumbarīṃ minoti | ūrjam eva madhyato dadhāti yajamāne ca prajāsu ca tasmān madhyataḥ prajā ūrg ūrjayati | asmai vai lokāyaudumbarī mīyate 'muṣmai yūpas tasmād itaḥ parāñcaṃ yūpaṃ prokṣaty amuto 'rvācīm audumbarīm anayor lokayor vidhṛtyai | ūrg vā udumbaras | yad amuto 'rvācīm audumbarīṃ prokṣati | amuta evārvācīm ūrjaṃ cyāvayati | asminn eva loka ūrjaṃ nyanakti prajāpater vā udgātorg udumbaryāṃ śrayate prajāsv evorjaṃ nyanakti devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ity abhrim ādatte savitṛprasūta evainaṃ devatābhir ādatte | idam ahaṃ rakṣaso grīvā apikṛntāmīti bhrātṛvyo vai rakṣas | bhrātṛvyasyaiva grīvā apikṛntati | śundhantāṃ lokāḥ pitṛṣadanā iti śundhaty evainām atho yad evāsya khanantaḥ krūraṃ kurvanti tac chamayati yavamatīr avasiñcati | annaṃ vai yavā ūrg udumbaras | anna evorjaṃ dadhāti pitṛṣadanaṃ tvā lokam āstṛṇāmīti yad vā etām apabarhiṣaṃ minuyur gartamit syāt | asyā uttarārdha oṣadhayo 'syā evainam uttarārdhe minoti | agartamitam evākar ud dyāṃ stabhānāntarikṣaṃ pṛṇa dṛṃhasva pṛthivyām iti dṛṃhaty evainām | nitānas tvā māruto nihantv iti mano vai nitānaḥ prāṇā mārutās svayaivaināṃ devatayāvaharati | nitāno ha sma vai māruto devānām audumbarīṃ minoti tenaivaināṃ minoti mitrāvaruṇayor dhruveṇa dharmaṇeti mitreṇa vā imāḥ prajāś śāntā varuṇena vidhṛtāḥ kḷptyā eva vidhṛtyai brahmavaniṃ tvā kṣatravanim iti | āśiṣam evāśāste brahma dṛṃha kṣatraṃ dṛṃheti | āśiṣam evāsmā āśiṣṭāṃ dṛṃhati ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī āpṛṇethām iti ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī vyunatti tasmād oṣadhayo 'nabhyaktā rebhante ghṛtenaudumbarīm abhijuhoti tejo vai ghṛtam annam udumbaras | anna eva tejo dadhāti | āntam eva vanaspatiṣu cauṣadhiṣu ca rasaṃ dadhāti | viśvajanasya cchāyāsīti viśvajanasya hy eṣā chāyā gotrādgotrād dhy etat saṃprasarpanti | audumbarīm abhi cchadīṃṣi saṃmukhāni kuryāt | daivīr vā etā viśo yad oṣadhayas | oṣadhayaś chadīṃṣi yajamāna audumbarī yajamānam eva prajā abhi saṃmukhāḥ karoti cchadir bhavati | athāntarvartas tasmāt puruṣasya māṃsam atha parśus | udaraṃ vā etad yajñasya yat sadas tiryaṅ minvanti tasmāt puruṣe 'śitaṃ dhriyate yad anvaṅ minuyur na puruṣe 'śitaṃ dhriyeta puruṣeṇa vai yajñas saṃmito yajñena puruṣas | yat sada ubhayataśchidram | tasmāt puruṣa ubhayataśchidras | viṣīvyanti tasmāt puruṣo 'ntarato viṣyūtas | indrasya syūr asīndrasya dhruvo 'sīti | aindraṃ vai sadas svayaiva devatayā sīvyati svayā devatayā granthiṃ grathnāti | aindram asīndrāya tveti saṃmitam abhimantrayate | aindraṃ vai sadas svayaivainaṃ devatayā samardhayati |
